panels.title: Is the operator reconciling at all
Reconcile errors (since start)
panels.description: Cumulative and exact. increase() extrapolates across scrape boundaries, so counting discrete events with it yields fractional answers — this panel read "2.26 errors" against a true count of 2. A count that cannot be true undermines every other number on the page, so the rate lives in its own panel and this one stays integral.

panels.title: Reconciles per second by controller
panels.description: Split by controller so a silent one is visible. An aggregate line stays healthy while a single controller has stopped.

panels.title: Workqueue depth by controller
panels.description: Every reconciler in this operator runs at the controller-runtime default of MaxConcurrentReconciles=1, so the queue drains serially. Depth is where a per-item cost that grows with cluster size becomes visible before latency does.

panels.title: Reconcile error rate
panels.description: The cumulative stat cannot say whether errors are still happening. A counter that stopped moving an hour ago looks identical to one incrementing now. Rate answers that; the stat answers how many.

panels.title: Unhealthy-node taint transitions
panels.description: applied and removed are plotted separately on purpose. A net count would sit at zero through a node flapping in and out of quarantine, which is the case worth seeing.

panels.title: Taint transitions since start
panels.description: Cumulative, so the chaos run's applied/removed pair is still readable after the rate window has passed.

panels.title: Quota drift corrections
panels.description: A ResourceQuota edited away from its GPUQuotaPolicy and put back. Sustained non-zero means something outside the operator is fighting it.

panels.title: MLTrainingJob phase transitions
panels.description: Transitions, not current occupancy: this counter increments on change, so a flat line means nothing is moving rather than nothing exists.

panels.title: Failed jobs by reason
panels.description: Reason is carried because 'a job failed' is not actionable and 'a job failed because its quota is gone' is.

panels.title: How long a tenant waited between having quota and using it
panels.description: The quantity the platform bounds and never used to report. GPUQuotaPolicy lends an idle tenant's quota within the cohort and takes it back by preemption, and the admission webhook caps a borrower's terminationGracePeriodSeconds at 120 because reclaim waits for termination. Those bound the worst case. This is the actual one. queuelab measured 2.180s when a preempted borrower honoured SIGTERM and 31.213s when it ignored it, which is why p50 and p99 are shown apart: a mean between those two describes neither.

panels.title: Waits the controller could not measure
panels.description: Read this beside the panel to its left, never instead of it. A quiet latency panel has two causes that look identical -- nothing ran, or everything ran and nothing was watching -- and only this one tells them apart. A rising AdmissionNotObserved means the controller was restarting across admissions and the wait it is not reporting could be any length at all.

panels.title: Reconcile duration p99 by controller
panels.description: p99 rather than a mean. The cost this operator was measured to have — an unindexed lookup proportional to the objects in a namespace — shows up in the tail long before it moves an average.

panels.title: Requests per second by final status code
panels.description: requests_total is stamped once per request with the status the client got, refusals before any backend (401, 403, 429) included. Split by code, not totalled: a gateway returning 500s at full rate is indistinguishable from a healthy one on a request-rate panel. A response cut short after it started is counted here under the 2xx it had already sent; the cut-short panel below is the only place it shows.

panels.title: End-to-end request duration p99 and p50
panels.description: Whole-request duration, observed when the handler returns, over requests handed to a backend. For a stream it runs until the stream closes, so it is dominated by output length and is neither TTFB nor TTFT. Both quantiles, because a p99 alone cannot say whether a spike hit every request or only the tail.

defaults.noValue: no series: no request handed to a backend

panels.title: Requests that ended in 5xx (final status)
panels.description: What the client got: requests_total with a 5xx final status, one count per request however many backends were tried. This is the series GatewayUpstreamErrorsReachingClients reads, over the same 5m window; it fires above 0.1 per second held for 5m. It includes 5xx the gateway wrote itself (502 and 504 when no backend answered, 503 when the request record could not be written). No series means no request has ended in 5xx since the gateway started, not a measured zero.

panels.title: Gateway time to first byte (TTFB) p99 and p50, not TTFT
panels.description: Time until the first response byte reached the client, over requests that produced one, including the 502 and 504 the gateway wrote itself. On a stream the status line and headers come before the first token, so this is a lower bound on TTFT and is not TTFT. TPOT is not measured by the gateway and has no panel.

defaults.noValue: no series: no first byte observed

panels.title: Failed backend attempts and fallback rescues
panels.description: upstream_errors_total counts failed ATTEMPTS, including the ones a later backend then rescued, so a request whose two attempts both failed counts twice; it is not what reached the client (the final 5xx panel is). backend_fallbacks_total counts requests a later backend answered 2xx or 3xx after an earlier one failed. Attempts rising with rescues keeping pace is redundancy absorbing the failures; attempts rising alone, with final 5xx rising, is the model failing.

defaults.noValue: no series: no failed attempt or rescue since start

panels.title: Responses cut short after starting (no status label)
panels.description: Responses that had started and ended before their upstream finished them, by cause: upstream_aborted (the engine died or dropped the connection), client_gone, idle_timeout. The status line was already sent, so requests_total counts each of these under the 2xx it had, and this counter carries no status label. It is the only series where a stream cut by an engine Pod dying mid-response shows up.

defaults.noValue: no series: no response cut short since start

panels.title: Rate limiting and admission decisions
panels.description: Refusals the gateway made on purpose, kept apart from upstream failures above. Conflating deliberate rejection with breakage is how a working limiter gets paged as an outage.

defaults.noValue: no series: no refusal or decision recorded
